title: Refresh a golden to host-supported harness CLIs
summary: A golden restores the harness CLIs it captured, so a QA plan's first golden reset on each Test Machine compares the versions recorded beside the golden with each vendor's latest release. A current golden costs one record read: no reset, install or capture. A golden that is behind, or has no record, is refreshed once for that plan under the plan's own host lease: reset, install the newer releases with each vendor's installer as the test user, capture through the ordinary golden capture (which keeps logins, keychains and cookies out), then begin the case again so every later reset restores the refreshed golden. Every installed CLI must run --version (in the GUI session on macOS). A binary that cannot run is held back: restore a runnable prior executable, or the newest runnable retained Cursor release, and report the requested version, exit code, stderr and selected version before capturing it. For held-back Cursor, run the retained vendor CLI set-channel static command so real requests cannot replace its launcher links; preserve other CLI config keys. Yoke's vendor installer still retries the latest release on later plans. Held-back versions are accepted for that host during the plan; actual versions stay in the existing sidecar, so later plans may retry the release without new Yoke settings. With no runnable version, or another failed step, stop with the harness diagnostic, a golden_refresh_* reason and its repair. A refused abort preserves the original runner error alongside the abort refusal. Old snapshots left after a verified refresh capture only warn with golden_snapshot_retention_failed, the host's own error and the cleanup; the plan continues because the next capture's space check still refuses a crowded disk. Agents and operators do not hand-update CLIs for QA; a hand-captured golden after an update remains the recovery when the serving control plane predates the plan_execution_id golden-capture argument. A verified hand capture whose recorded CLIs are behind latest warns golden_harness_clis_behind_latest, naming each behind CLI, because the next plan's refresh replaces that golden; an unreachable release channel warns golden_harness_latest_unavailable and the capture stands.
